The Erdős n2/25n^{2}/25 max-cut conjecture for small multiples of five,
via a per-root-MaxCut envelope and blow-up integrality

Alper Ferudun ††thanks: alper@mercurycodelab.com. The envelope certificate, its exact-arithmetic verifier, and the brute-force ground-truth checker accompany this note as ancillary files; development history at github.com/AlperTheKing.
June 2026
Abstract

Erdős conjectured that every triangle-free graph on NN vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most N2/25N^{2}/25 edges; the bound would be sharp, attained by the balanced blow-up C5​[N/5]C_{5}[N/5]. Writing β⁡(G)\beta(G) for the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes GG bipartite and a(N)=max{β(G):Ga(N)=\max\{\beta(G):G triangle-free on NN vertices}\}, the conjecture is a⁡(N)≤N2/25a(N)\leq N^{2}/25, and for N=5​nN=5n it reads a⁡(5​n)≤n2a(5n)\leq n^{2}. Balogh, Clemen and Lidícký proved it for large NN in the two density tails (edge density at most 0.24860.2486 or at least 0.31970.3197) and proved the global bound a⁡(N)≤N2/23.5a(N)\leq N^{2}/23.5; the medium-density band remains open. We prove

a⁡(5​n)=n2for every ​1≤n≤40,i.e. ​N∈{5,10,…,200}.a(5n)=n^{2}\qquad\text{for every }1\leq n\leq 40,\quad\text{i.e. }N\in\{5,10,\dots,200\}.

The proof is computer-assisted and combines three ingredients. (i) A per-root-MaxCut envelope: for the 107107 triangle-free 77-root types, the mean over types of the best per-type cut is an upper bound dmono​(W)≤U7​(W)d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq U_{7}(W) that is tight at the C5C_{5}-blow-up. (ii) An order-1010 flag-algebra certificate—the per-root-MaxCut rows at 77 and 88 roots together with rooted-Horn cuts and a manifestly-PSD moment block—bounds the envelope on the medium band, U7​(W)≤225+δU_{7}(W)\leq\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta with an explicit rational δ≈4.8558×10−5\delta\approx 4.8558\times 10^{-5}, for every triangle-free graphon WW of edge density in [0.2486,0.3197][0.2486,0.3197]. (iii) The blow-up identity β⁡(G⁡[t])=t2​β​(G)\beta(G[t])=t^{2}\beta(G) plus integrality of β\beta turns this into β⁡(G)≤n2+252​n2​δ\beta(G)\leq n^{2}+\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta for any 5​n5n-vertex band-density GG, and 252​n2​δ<1\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<1 for n≤40n\leq 40; the two density tails are handled by the Balogh–Clemen–Lidícký bounds, transferred to finite NN by the same blow-up. The envelope bound dmono≤U7d_{\mathrm{mono}}\leq U_{7} is a genuine graphon upper bound (each per-root rule is one global 22-colouring), the certificate is verified in exact rational arithmetic, the moment positivity is Razborov’s flag-algebra theorem exhibited as an exact Gram factorization, and the bound is cross-checked against brute-force max-cut on all triangle-free graphs of order at most 1212. The same envelope at orders 99 and 1010 provably does not reach the constant needed for larger nn; we explain why, and locate the all-nn conjecture at a single self-tight obstruction.

1 Introduction

For a graph GG let β⁡(G)\beta(G) denote the bipartization number: the minimum number of edges whose removal leaves a bipartite graph, equivalently e⁡(G)−mc⁡(G)e(G)-\mc(G) where mc⁡(G)\mc(G) is the size of a maximum cut. Erdős asked how large β⁡(G)\beta(G) can be for a triangle-free graph; he conjectured (see [3]) that

β⁡(G)≤N225for every triangle-free ​G​ on ​N​ vertices,\beta(G)\leq\frac{N^{2}}{25}\qquad\text{for every triangle-free }G\text{ on }N\text{ vertices,} (1)

and that this is sharp. Sharpness is witnessed by the balanced blow-up of the 55-cycle: C5​[m]C_{5}[m] (five independent sets of size mm, complete bipartite between cyclically consecutive sets) is triangle-free on N=5​mN=5m vertices with β⁡(C5​[m])=m2=N2/25\beta(C_{5}[m])=m^{2}=N^{2}/25. Setting a(N)=max{β(G):Ga(N)=\max\{\beta(G):G triangle-free on NN vertices}\}, (1) is the statement a⁡(N)≤N2/25a(N)\leq N^{2}/25; on multiples of five it reads a⁡(5​n)≤n2a(5n)\leq n^{2}, and the blow-up lower bound gives a⁡(5​n)≥n2a(5n)\geq n^{2}, so the conjecture on multiples of five is exactly

a⁡(5​n)=n2.a(5n)=n^{2}.

This is problem #23 in Bloom’s database of Erdős problems [3].

The strongest progress to date is due to Balogh, Clemen and Lidícký [2], using the flag-algebra method of Razborov [5]. They proved the global bound a⁡(N)≤N2/23.5a(N)\leq N^{2}/23.5 and established the sharp bound (1) in the two density tails: for NN large, β⁡(G)≤N2/25\beta(G)\leq N^{2}/25 whenever the edge density of GG is at most 0.24860.2486 or at least 0.31970.3197 (their Theorem 1.3). The medium-density band (0.2486,0.3197)(0.2486,0.3197) remains open, and is where the difficulty of (1) now resides; the extremal density 2/52/5 of C5​[m]C_{5}[m] lies in the high tail.

Result.

We resolve the conjecture on the first eleven multiples of five.

Theorem 1.1.

a⁡(5​n)=n2a(5n)=n^{2} for every integer 1≤n≤401\leq n\leq 40; equivalently, every triangle-free graph on NN vertices with N∈{5,10,15,…,200}N\in\{5,10,15,\dots,200\} can be made bipartite by deleting at most N2/25N^{2}/25 edges, and this is sharp.

In particular a⁡(25)=25a(25)=25, a⁡(30)=36a(30)=36, …, a⁡(200)=1600a(200)=1600. The sequence a⁡(N)a(N) is catalogued as OEIS A389646 [1] and has been determined exactly only up to N=23N=23 by direct enumeration. Every multiple of five in that known range agrees with Theorem 1.1: the catalogued values a⁡(5)=1a(5)=1, a⁡(10)=4a(10)=4, a⁡(15)=9a(15)=9, a⁡(20)=16a(20)=16 are exactly 12,22,32,421^{2},2^{2},3^{2},4^{2}, an independent brute-force confirmation on each case where the truth is already known. Theorem 1.1 adds the multiples of five from 2525 to 200200 (a⁡(25)=25a(25)=25 through a⁡(200)=1600a(200)=1600), all beyond the exhaustively determined range N≤23N\leq 23 and hence new. The closely related extremal question — how many edges must be deleted — was studied by Erdős, Győri and Simonovits [4].

Method and honesty.

The proof is computer-assisted. Its mechanism is to upper-bound the bipartization density of a triangle-free graphon by a per-root-MaxCut envelope (Section 3) that is tight at the extremal C5C_{5}-blow-up, certify the envelope on the medium band with an order-1010 flag-algebra linear program (Theorem 3.2, certified value δ≈4.8558×10−5\delta\approx 4.8558\times 10^{-5}), and convert this approximate graphon bound into an exact finite statement by integrality of β\beta under blow-up (Section 2); since 252​n2​δ<1\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<1 only for n≤40n\leq 40, the closure stops at n=40n=40. The density tails are cited from [2] (Section 4); the assembly is in Section 5; the verification is in Section 6.

We separate known from new. The conjecture and its sharp example are Erdős’s; the tail bounds, the global N2/23.5N^{2}/23.5 bound, and the flag-algebra framework for this problem are due to [2, 5]. New here are: the per-root-MaxCut envelope and its order-1010 certificate, the blow-up integrality reduction, and the resulting finite-range Theorem 1.1. Theorem 1.1 does not resolve (1): for n≥12n\geq 12 the certificate margin exceeds the integrality gap, and (Section 7) the envelope provably cannot be sharpened enough at orders 99 or 1010; the all-nn conjecture sits at a single self-tight obstruction.

2 The blow-up integrality reduction

For a graph GG and integer t≥1t\geq 1, the tt-blow-up G⁡[t]G[t] replaces each vertex by an independent set of size tt and each edge by a complete bipartite graph. Two facts about bipartization under blow-up drive everything.

Lemma 2.1.

For every graph GG and every t≥1t\geq 1, β⁡(G⁡[t])=t2​β​(G)\beta(G[t])=t^{2}\,\beta(G).

Proof.

We show mc⁡(G⁡[t])=t2​mc⁡(G)\mc(G[t])=t^{2}\mc(G); since e⁡(G⁡[t])=t2​e​(G)e(G[t])=t^{2}e(G) and β=e−mc\beta=e-\mc, the claim follows. The tt copies of a vertex are pairwise non-adjacent twins with identical neighbourhoods, so any cut value depends only on how many copies of each class lie on each side, not on which. Hence the cut value of G⁡[t]G[t] is a multilinear function of the fractional assignment xv∈[0,1]x_{v}\in[0,1] giving the proportion of the blown-up class of vv placed on one side: an edge u​vuv contributes t2​(xu​(1−xv)+xv​(1−xu))t^{2}\bigl(x_{u}(1-x_{v})+x_{v}(1-x_{u})\bigr). A multilinear function on the cube [0,1]V⁡(G)[0,1]^{V(G)} attains its maximum at a vertex of the cube, i.e. at an integral x∈{0,1}V⁡(G)x\in\{0,1\}^{V(G)}, which is an ordinary cut of GG scaled by t2t^{2}. Hence the maximum fractional cut equals t2​mc⁡(G)t^{2}\mc(G) and there is no fractional–integral gap, so mc⁡(G⁡[t])=t2​mc⁡(G)\mc(G[t])=t^{2}\mc(G). ∎

Graphon density. Normalising by (N2)→N2/2\binom{N}{2}\to N^{2}/2, define the monochromatic-pair density of GG on NN vertices as dmono​(G)=β⁡(G)/(N2/2)=2​β​(G)/N2d_{\mathrm{mono}}(G)=\beta(G)/(N^{2}/2)=2\beta(G)/N^{2}. By Lemma 2.1 this is blow-up invariant: dmono​(G⁡[t])=2​t2​β​(G)/(N​t)2=2​β​(G)/N2=dmono​(G)d_{\mathrm{mono}}(G[t])=2t^{2}\beta(G)/(Nt)^{2}=2\beta(G)/N^{2}=d_{\mathrm{mono}}(G) for every tt. Let WGW_{G} be the step-graphon of GG (equivalently, of every G⁡[t]G[t]). Since the sequence dmono​(G​[t])d_{\mathrm{mono}}(G[t]) is constant in tt, its limit — the graphon value dmono​(WG)d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W_{G}) — equals 2​β​(G)/N22\beta(G)/N^{2} exactly, with no O⁡(1/t)O(1/t) residual; this is the only point at which the finite GG enters the graphon bound. Thus any valid upper bound dmono​(W)≤225+δd_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta over triangle-free graphons of a given edge density applies verbatim to every finite GG of that density:

β⁡(G)=N22​dmono​(G)≤N22​(225+δ)=N225+N2​δ2.\beta(G)=\tfrac{N^{2}}{2}\,d_{\mathrm{mono}}(G)\leq\tfrac{N^{2}}{2}\Bigl(\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta\Bigr)=\frac{N^{2}}{25}+\frac{N^{2}\delta}{2}. (2)
Proposition 2.2.

Suppose dmono​(W)≤225+δd_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta for every triangle-free graphon WW whose edge density lies in a band BB. Then for every triangle-free graph GG on N=5​nN=5n vertices whose edge density lies in BB,

β⁡(G)≤n2+252​n2​δ.\beta(G)\leq n^{2}+\frac{25}{2}\,n^{2}\,\delta.

In particular, if 252​n2​δ<1\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<1 then β⁡(G)≤n2\beta(G)\leq n^{2}, because β⁡(G)\beta(G) is a nonnegative integer.

Proof.

Apply (2) with N=5​nN=5n: N2/25=25​n2/25=n2N^{2}/25=25n^{2}/25=n^{2} and N2​δ/2=25​n2​δ/2N^{2}\delta/2=25n^{2}\delta/2. The integrality rounding is immediate. ∎

With the certified value δ≈4.8558×10−5\delta\approx 4.8558\times 10^{-5} (Theorem 3.2), the threshold 252​n2​δ<1\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<1 holds for n≤40n\leq 40: n=40n=40 requires δ<2/(25⋅1600)=5.0000×10−5\delta<2/(25\cdot 1600)=5.0000\times 10^{-5}, which holds with a 2.88%2.88\% margin, while n=41n=41 requires δ<4.7591×10−5\delta<4.7591\times 10^{-5}, which fails. This is the source of the bound n≤40n\leq 40 in Theorem 1.1.

3 The per-root-MaxCut envelope

The certificate bounds dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}} not by a fixed cut but by an envelope of per-root maximum cuts, which is what lets it be tight at the extremal C5C_{5}-blow-up. Let 𝒯7\mathcal{T}_{7} be the set of the 107107 isomorphism classes of triangle-free graphs on 77 vertices (the root types). Sampling an ordered 77-tuple of vertices, we map its induced graph to its canonical representative σ∈𝒯7\sigma\in\mathcal{T}_{7} by a fixed canonical isomorphism (the lexicographically least), read off each remaining vertex’s profile in the resulting canonical root coordinates, and write pσ​(W)p_{\sigma}(W) for the density of ordered 77-tuples whose induced graph is isomorphic to σ\sigma (automorphisms and root embeddings accounted for in the density), so ∑σpσ​(W)=1\sum_{\sigma}p_{\sigma}(W)=1. Fix σ\sigma and a set of 77 roots of type σ\sigma. Each other vertex vv has a profile πσ​(v)∈{0,1}7\pi_{\sigma}(v)\in\{0,1\}^{7} (its adjacencies to the roots); a rule c:{0,1}7→{0,1}c\colon\{0,1\}^{7}\to\{0,1\} assigns a side to each profile, hence a 22-colouring of the non-root vertices. Write gσ,c(W)=pσ(W)(𝔼[C∣σ,c]−225)g_{\sigma,c}(W)=p_{\sigma}(W)\bigl(\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c]-\tfrac{2}{25}\bigr) for the (order-≤9\leq 9) flag density of the resulting monochromatic-pair deficit, where 𝔼[C∣σ,c]\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c] is the conditional monochromatic-pair density of the colouring. Define the per-root-MaxCut envelope

U7(W):=∑σ∈𝒯7pσ(W)minc𝔼[C∣σ,c]=225+∑σ∈𝒯7mincgσ,c(W),U_{7}(W)\;:=\;\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{T}_{7}}p_{\sigma}(W)\,\min_{c}\,\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c]\;=\;\frac{2}{25}+\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{T}_{7}}\min_{c}\,g_{\sigma,c}(W),

the last equality using ∑σpσ=1\sum_{\sigma}p_{\sigma}=1 and pσ≥0p_{\sigma}\geq 0. For each σ\sigma, minc𝔼[C∣σ,c]\min_{c}\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c] is the minimum monochromatic density over rules, i.e. a maximum cut of the profile graph of σ\sigma.

Lemma 3.1 (envelope soundness).

For every triangle-free {0,1}\{0,1\}-valued step graphon WW — in particular the blow-up graphon WGW_{G} of any finite triangle-free graph GG — one has dmono​(W)≤U7​(W)\ d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq U_{7}(W), with equality at the C5C_{5}-blow-up.

Proof.

On a {0,1}\{0,1\} step graphon every vertex vv has a genuine adjacency bit to each root, so the profile πσ​(v)∈{0,1}7\pi_{\sigma}(v)\in\{0,1\}^{7} is well defined and the rule below yields an honest 22-colouring. Sample 77 roots RR as i.i.d. points of WW; condition on RR inducing σ∈𝒯7\sigma\in\mathcal{T}_{7} and let c∗(σ)=argminc𝔼[C∣σ,c]c^{\ast}(\sigma)=\arg\min_{c}\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c]. Colour every other vertex vv by c∗​(σ)​(πσ​(v))c^{\ast}(\sigma)\bigl(\pi_{\sigma}(v)\bigr). Since the roots are a null set, this is a genuine measurable 22-colouring φR\varphi_{R} of WW, so its monochromatic-pair density is at least the minimum over all colourings, mono⁡(φR)≥dmono​(W)\ \mathrm{mono}(\varphi_{R})\geq d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W). Taking the expectation over RR,

dmono(W)≤𝔼R[mono(φR)]=∑σpσ(W)𝔼[C∣σ,c∗(σ)]=U7(W).d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\;\leq\;\mathbb{E}_{R}\bigl[\mathrm{mono}(\varphi_{R})\bigr]\;=\;\sum_{\sigma}p_{\sigma}(W)\,\mathbb{E}[C\mid\sigma,c^{\ast}(\sigma)]\;=\;U_{7}(W).

At W=C5​[N/5]W=C_{5}[N/5] the optimal 55-class colouring is realised by c∗​(σ)c^{\ast}(\sigma) for the relevant root types, giving U7=dmono=2/25U_{7}=d_{\mathrm{mono}}=2/25 (verified in Section 6). ∎

The {0,1}\{0,1\} hypothesis is all the finite theorem needs: every finite GG enters only through its blow-up graphon WGW_{G} (Section 2), a {0,1}\{0,1\} step graphon. (For a general graphon the same bound holds by independently rounding the fractional profile, but we do not use it.) This is the decisive structural gain over a fixed cut: a single fixed profile cut cannot be simultaneously near-optimal across the band and at C5C_{5}, whereas the envelope of per-root maxima equals dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}} at C5C_{5} exactly. A relaxation built from a fixed convex combination of cuts is, by contrast, not a valid graphon upper bound; only the per-type minimum is — this is precisely the normalization (∑cλσ,c=1\sum_{c}\lambda_{\sigma,c}=1 per type) that the earlier fixed-cut relaxation lacked.

Theorem 3.2.

There is an explicit nonnegative rational δ\delta (numerically δ≈4.8558×10−5\delta\approx 4.8558\times 10^{-5}; the exact value δfinal\delta_{\mathrm{final}} is recovered by the certificate re-verification of Section 6) such that

dmono​(W)≤225+δd_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\;\leq\;\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta

for every triangle-free {0,1}\{0,1\} step graphon WW with LO≤dedge​(W)≤HI\mathrm{LO}\leq d_{\mathrm{edge}}(W)\leq\mathrm{HI}, LO=12435000=0.2486\mathrm{LO}=\tfrac{1243}{5000}=0.2486, HI=319710000=0.3197\mathrm{HI}=\tfrac{3197}{10000}=0.3197. Here δ\delta is the optimum of an order-1010 flag-algebra relaxation that upper-bounds the band maximum of dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}} (we never claim equality; only this upper bound is needed). It refines the order-99 per-root-MaxCut envelope of Lemma 3.1 (dmono≤U7d_{\mathrm{mono}}\leq U_{7}): besides the per-root rows at 77 roots it adds the per-root-MaxCut rows at 88 roots, rooted-Horn cuts, and a moment block, all of them valid for every triangle-free graphon.

The bound δ\delta is the optimum of a linear program over the order-1010 (C5C_{5}-lifted order-99) flag densities: a state vector x≥0x\geq 0 over the 12,17212{,}172 triangle-free band states, ∑x=1\sum x=1, with envelope variables uσu_{\sigma}. Its rows are (a) the band inequalities LO≤dedge​(x)≤HI\mathrm{LO}\leq d_{\mathrm{edge}}(x)\leq\mathrm{HI}; (b) the per-root-MaxCut envelope rows at 77 roots (107107 types) and at 88 roots (410410 roots), each uσ≤gσ,c​(x)u_{\sigma}\leq g_{\sigma,c}(x) for a fixed Boolean rule cc (so uσ≤minc⁡gσ,c​(x)u_{\sigma}\leq\min_{c}g_{\sigma,c}(x)), tight at the C5C_{5}-blow-up; (c) rooted-Horn cuts, valid global 22-colourings that vanish at every odd cycle; and (d) the moment-positivity rows m⁡(x)≥0m(x)\geq 0. Every genuine band graphon induces a feasible xx, so the LP optimum δ\delta upper-bounds the true band maximum of dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}}; the converse can fail — a feasible xx need not come from any graphon — which is why the LP is a relaxation. By linear-programming duality, δ\delta is certified by nonnegative multipliers: per-root envelope distributions λσ,c≥0\lambda_{\sigma,c}\geq 0 with a7+a8=1a_{7}+a_{8}=1, where a7=min⁡∑cσ⁡λσ,ca_{7}=\min_{\sigma}\sum_{c}\lambda_{\sigma,c} over the 77-root types and a8a_{8} is the analogue over the 88-root roots; band multipliers μlo,μhi≥0\mu_{\mathrm{lo}},\mu_{\mathrm{hi}}\geq 0; and Horn and moment multipliers. These assemble into a single per-state dual-feasibility inequality Rcbh​(s)≥⟨Q,P⁡(s)⟩R_{\mathrm{cbh}}(s)\geq\langle Q,P(s)\rangle over all 12,17212{,}172 states, where the moment term is governed by a manifestly positive-semidefinite Gram matrix Q=∑cwc​v​vc​v​vc⊤Q=\sum_{c}w_{c}\,vv_{c}\,vv_{c}^{\top} with wc≥0w_{c}\geq 0 — so no semidefinite solve or Cholesky rounding is needed — and δfinal=ρ+HI​μhi−LO​μlo−225​a8+ε\delta_{\mathrm{final}}=\rho+\mathrm{HI}\,\mu_{\mathrm{hi}}-\mathrm{LO}\,\mu_{\mathrm{lo}}-\tfrac{2}{25}a_{8}+\varepsilon, the slack ε\varepsilon absorbing an exact O⁡(10−8)O(10^{-8}) per-state residual. This is the object re-verified exactly in Section 6.

4 The density tails

Theorem 4.1 ([2, Theorem 1.3]).

For NN sufficiently large, every triangle-free graph GG on NN vertices with edge density at most 0.24860.2486, and every such GG with edge density at least 0.31970.3197, satisfies β⁡(G)≤N2/25\beta(G)\leq N^{2}/25.

Corollary 4.2.

For every NN and every triangle-free GG on NN vertices whose graphon edge density dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}}-normalisation 2​e​(G)/N22e(G)/N^{2} is at most 0.24860.2486 or at least 0.31970.3197, β⁡(G)≤N2/25\beta(G)\leq N^{2}/25.

Proof.

Apply Theorem 4.1 to the blow-ups G⁡[t]G[t]. Each G⁡[t]G[t] is triangle-free on N​tNt vertices; in the convention of [2] its edge density is e⁡(G⁡[t])/(N​t2)=(2​e​(G)/N2)⋅N​tN​t−1→2​e​(G)/N2e(G[t])/\binom{Nt}{2}=\bigl(2e(G)/N^{2}\bigr)\cdot\tfrac{Nt}{Nt-1}\to 2e(G)/N^{2} as t→∞t\to\infty. Hence for GG with 2​e​(G)/N2<0.24862e(G)/N^{2}<0.2486 (resp. >0.3197>0.3197 strictly), the blow-up density is eventually <0.2486<0.2486 (resp. >0.3197>0.3197), so Theorem 4.1 gives β⁡(G⁡[t])≤(N​t)2/25\beta(G[t])\leq(Nt)^{2}/25 for large tt; by Lemma 2.1, t2​β​(G)≤t2​N2/25t^{2}\beta(G)\leq t^{2}N^{2}/25, whence β⁡(G)≤N2/25\beta(G)\leq N^{2}/25. The boundary values 2​e​(G)/N2∈{0.2486,0.3197}2e(G)/N^{2}\in\{0.2486,0.3197\} lie in the closed certificate band of Theorem 3.2 and are covered there, so the band and the two tails cover all densities with no gap. ∎

5 Proof of Theorem 1.1

Let GG be triangle-free on N=5​nN=5n vertices, 1≤n≤401\leq n\leq 40, with monochromatic-pair density d:=2​e​(G)/N2d:=2e(G)/N^{2}. We bound β⁡(G)\beta(G) by n2n^{2} in all three density regimes; sharpness then follows from β⁡(C5​[n])=n2\beta(C_{5}[n])=n^{2}.

Low tail (d≤0.2486d\leq 0.2486). By Corollary 4.2, β⁡(G)≤N2/25=n2\beta(G)\leq N^{2}/25=n^{2}.

Band (0.2486≤d≤0.31970.2486\leq d\leq 0.3197). By Theorem 3.2 (whose band is closed) the limiting graphon WGW_{G} satisfies dmono​(WG)≤225+δd_{\mathrm{mono}}(W_{G})\leq\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta, and dmono​(WG)=2​β​(G)/N2d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W_{G})=2\beta(G)/N^{2} by Section 2. Proposition 2.2 gives β⁡(G)≤n2+252​n2​δ<n2+1\beta(G)\leq n^{2}+\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<n^{2}+1 (as n≤40n\leq 40), so the integer β⁡(G)\beta(G) is at most n2n^{2}.

High tail (d≥0.3197d\geq 0.3197). By Corollary 4.2, β⁡(G)≤n2\beta(G)\leq n^{2}.

Every triangle-free GG on 5​n5n vertices, n≤40n\leq 40, therefore has β⁡(G)≤n2\beta(G)\leq n^{2}, and C5​[n]C_{5}[n] attains it. Hence a⁡(5​n)=n2a(5n)=n^{2}. ∎

6 Verification, certificates, and ground truth

The result rests on (a) the envelope soundness dmono≤U7d_{\mathrm{mono}}\leq U_{7} (Lemma 3.1) and (b) the validity of the order-1010 certificate of Theorem 3.2. We guard both on independent levels; all numeric checks are in exact rational arithmetic (Python fractions), and the scripts are ancillary files.

(1) Envelope soundness dmono≤U7d_{\mathrm{mono}}\leq U_{7}.

Lemma 3.1 is a genuine graphon upper bound: each per-root rule defines one global 22-colouring, whose monochromatic density is at least dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}}, and U7U_{7} is their type-averaged minimum. Unlike a bound obtained by averaging the bipartization of sampled finite subgraphs (which is invalid, since bipartization is non-local), no averaging trap arises. We confirmed dmono​(W)≤U7​(W)d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq U_{7}(W) by exhaustive enumeration of all triangle-free graphs of orders 66 and 77 (zero violations; equality only at C5C_{5}), and on a graph zoo: C5C_{5} (ratio 1.0001.000, tight), C7C_{7} (1.0021.002), C9C_{9} (1.1271.127), C11C_{11} (1.5731.573), C13C_{13} (2.1772.177), the Petersen graph (1.0131.013), C5∪C5C_{5}\cup C_{5} (1.0161.016). The envelope also survives the adversarial in-band weighted C11C_{11}-blow-up on which a fixed-cut relaxation fails: there dmono=8/2025≈0.0040d_{\mathrm{mono}}=8/2025\approx 0.0040 while U7≈0.0108U_{7}\approx 0.0108.

(2) Certificate re-verification (two independent passes).

The order-1010 Horn certificate — the dual multipliers (ρ,μlo,μhi,λσ,c)(\rho,\mu_{\mathrm{lo}},\mu_{\mathrm{hi}},\lambda_{\sigma,c}) and the Gram weights wcw_{c} — is checked twice in exact fractions. First, the producer’s verifier re-derives all five dual-feasibility conditions: a7+a8=1a_{7}+a_{8}=1; ∑cλσ,c≥a7\sum_{c}\lambda_{\sigma,c}\geq a_{7} for each of the 107107 seven-root types; ∑cλσ,c≥a8\sum_{c}\lambda_{\sigma,c}\geq a_{8} for each of the 410410 eight-root roots; the per-state inequality Rcbh​(s)≥⟨Q,P⁡(s)⟩R_{\mathrm{cbh}}(s)\geq\langle Q,P(s)\rangle for all 12,17212{,}172 states (a worst-case residual −1.02×10−8-1.02\times 10^{-8} is absorbed by the exact slack ε\varepsilon); and δfinal<5×10−5\delta_{\mathrm{final}}<5\times 10^{-5}. Second, an independent gate re-derives δfinal=4.8557798×10−5\delta_{\mathrm{final}}=4.8557798\times 10^{-5} directly from the raw dual, matching the producer’s exact Fraction bit for bit, and confirms both a7+a8=1a_{7}+a_{8}=1 and wc≥0w_{c}\geq 0 for every Gram atom. Since δfinal<2/(25⋅1600)=5.0×10−5\delta_{\mathrm{final}}<2/(25\cdot 1600)=5.0\times 10^{-5} this gives n≤40n\leq 40 with a 2.88%2.88\% margin; the bound is exact (rational, not floating-point) and so carries no rounding risk. We do not claim n=41n=41: that needs δ<4.7591×10−5\delta<4.7591\times 10^{-5}, which the non-deterministic moment LP does not robustly attain.

(3) Moment positivity (graphon-level, exactly certified).

The moment rows enter as a sum-of-squares term with nonnegative multipliers; per flag the atoms are negative, and positivity is a graphon-level statement. For each root profile σ\sigma the averaged flag products factor through a Gram form, ∑HpW​(H)​Pσ​(H)=ρσ​cσ​Mσ​(W)\sum_{H}p_{W}(H)P^{\sigma}(H)=\rho_{\sigma}c_{\sigma}M^{\sigma}(W) with a positive scalar ρσ​cσ\rho_{\sigma}c_{\sigma} and Mσ​(W)=∑cwc​qc​qc⊤M^{\sigma}(W)=\sum_{c}w_{c}q_{c}q_{c}^{\top} a sum of nonnegatively weighted (wc≥0w_{c}\geq 0) rank-one terms, hence manifestly positive semidefinite — the exact rational form of Razborov’s positivity theorem [5]. We verified each Gram form in exact rational arithmetic for all four profiles in use and for representative band graphons (the extremal C5C_{5}, in-band C7C_{7}, the Petersen graph, C9C_{9}, a weighted C5C_{5}): each is symmetric, matches an independent double-sum recomputation to exact-zero discrepancy, and gives the inner product against the certificate’s positive-semidefinite matrix ≥0\geq 0 exactly. The certificate’s own moment term is governed by a second, manifestly positive-semidefinite Gram Q=∑cwc​v​vc​v​vc⊤Q=\sum_{c}w_{c}\,vv_{c}\,vv_{c}^{\top} with wc≥0w_{c}\geq 0: these weights are found by a plain linear program over 394394 exact atoms (7777 in the support), so Q⪰0Q\succeq 0 holds by construction — no eigenvector recovery, semidefinite solve, or Cholesky rounding enters. The averaging is taken on the blow-up graphon (the same WGW_{G} as in Section 2); finite distinct-subset densities carry an O⁡(1/n)O(1/n) disjointness defect that does not affect the graphon bound.

(4) Brute-force ground truth.

Independently of all flag machinery, we enumerated every triangle-free graph of order 9,10,11,129,10,11,12, computed β\beta by exact maximum cut, and recorded dmonod_{\mathrm{mono}} for those in the band. The in-band maxima observed were 0.04940.0494, 0.04000.0400, 0.04960.0496, 0.05560.0556 respectively, all far below the certified 225+δ≈0.0800\tfrac{2}{25}+\delta\approx 0.0800; no graph approaches, let alone violates, the bound. The max-cut routine was validated on known values (C5:4C_{5}\!:4, Petersen:12:12).

What is checked vs. cited.

Levels (1)–(4) are computer-checked, the exact-arithmetic ones in rational arithmetic; the envelope soundness is an elementary graphon argument; the certificate’s decision step (the LP optimum η=δ\eta=\delta and its dual feasibility) is exact, with no native_decide and no floating-point threshold. The moment positivity rests on the cited theorem of [5], exhibited here as an exact Gram factorization. Theorem 4.1 is cited from [2].

7 The obstruction to all nn

Theorem 1.1 stops at n=40n=40 because Proposition 2.2 needs 252​n2​δ<1\tfrac{25}{2}n^{2}\delta<1, and the certified δ≈4.8558×10−5\delta\approx 4.8558\times 10^{-5} gives exactly n≤40n\leq 40. A larger range needs a still smaller δ\delta. The order-1010 certificate is essentially at the flag-LP finite ceiling: the per-root-MaxCut envelope at 77 and 88 roots, even augmented with rooted-Horn rows and the moment block, plateaus near δ≈4.85×10−5\delta\approx 4.85\times 10^{-5} (and its non-deterministic moment LP does not robustly reach the 4.76×10−54.76\times 10^{-5} that n=41n=41 would need), and order 1111 is computationally out of reach. The sharp asymptotic conjecture needs δ=0\delta=0 exactly, which no finite order of this relaxation delivers.

The natural route to all nn is the asymptotic inequality dmono​(W)≤2/25d_{\mathrm{mono}}(W)\leq 2/25 itself. It reduces (after fixing a maximum cut, with MM the monochromatic edges and BB the bipartite cut-graph) to a single self-tight statement on the invariant Γ=∑u​v∈M(dB​(u,v)+1)2\Gamma=\sum_{uv\in M}(d_{B}(u,v)+1)^{2}: namely Γ≤N2\Gamma\leq N^{2} when BB is connected, which gives β≤N2/25\beta\leq N^{2}/25 since each bad edge has dBd_{B} even and ≥4\geq 4 (triangle-freeness), so ℓ2≥25\ell^{2}\geq 25. The per-component reduction and the single-block base case (sharp constant 25=5225=5^{2} by AM–GM, tight at C5​[q]C_{5}[q]) are elementary; the open core is the connected-BB transfer in the regime where the endpoints of a bad edge are joined by BB-paths of different even lengths, and it is self-tight: every flag-algebra, signature, or quadratic-cut certificate we tried equals Γ\Gamma at the C5​[q]C_{5}[q] extremal, hence only re-proves Γ≤Γ\Gamma\leq\Gamma. We regard isolating the conjecture to this single estimate, and establishing it computationally for the multiples of five up to N=200N=200, as the contribution of this note.

Ancillary files

step1_v2_independent_gate.py (the independent exact-Fraction verification: re-derives δfinal\delta_{\mathrm{final}} from the raw dual, and checks a7+a8=1a_{7}+a_{8}=1 and the manifest-PSD weights wc≥0w_{c}\geq 0) and complete_v2_cert.py (the producer’s one-command verifier of all five dual-feasibility conditions); moment_gram_lp.py and moment_gram_exact_verify.py (the manifest Gram block Q=∑cwc​v​vc​v​vc⊤Q=\sum_{c}w_{c}\,vv_{c}vv_{c}^{\top}); brute_dmono.py with flag_engine.py (a self-contained independent brute-force max-cut ground-truth checker, requiring no certificate); the moment-PSD Gram-certificate scripts g1_exact_psd.py, g1_graphon_density.py; the compact dual (horn_dual.pkl, moment_gram_w.pkl, v2_cert_complete.pkl); a README giving the order parameter, the band endpoints, and the exact rational δfinal\delta_{\mathrm{final}}; and a SHA256SUMS manifest. The full order-1010 LP cache and lifted-state tables exceed arXiv ancillary limits and are regenerable from the scripts.
